blind_target.authors: Srinivasan, M., & Carey, S.
blind_target.title: The long and the short of it: On the nature and origin of functional overlap between representations of space and time.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The claim selected for replication from Srinivasan and Carey (2010) was the Experiment 3 claim that participants who were familiarised with congruent pairings of line lengths and tone duration (e.g., long line, long tone) spontaneously accessed the structural similarity between representations, allowing for precise encoding of these pairings, supporting more accurate detection of novel vs. familiar items, compared with participants familiarised with incongruent pairings (e.g., long line, short tone).
blind_target.outcome_quote: In the results quoted above, Srinivasan and Carey (2010) reported p-values for 11 effects. We replicated all seven that were p < .05. We observed p < .05 for the four effects that Srinivasan and Carey (2010) reported as non-significant. However the size and direction of our effects were consistent with the trends reported in the original paper.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The SCORE H* group-by-novelty claim is explicitly replicated, but this is one effect rather than an overall verdict. Preregistered additional analyses deliberately retest the first two paragraphs of original section 4.2; the side-by-side comparisons explicitly show incongruent participants detecting novelty where the original reported they did not, and the final paragraph identifies four original null findings becoming significant. Authors note consistent direction/trends and power as an explanation, yet explicitly identify these differences. This is not mixed merely because the main effect is smaller or because a measure count differs.

items.parent_scope_question: Determine authors own reading of four newly significant formerly-null effects. Magnitude/trends and statistical power alone do not mechanically make mixed; compare the original claims and any explicit contrast/overall verdict.

shipped.title_o: Beyond the double-jeopardy hypothesis: Assessing emotion on the faces of multiply-categorizable targets of prejudice
shipped.outcome_quote: "Our analyses revealed a significant two-way interaction between target age and target race, F(1, 54) = 20.92, p = .001, η²p = 0.28. In addition, analyses revealed a significant paired-samples t-test such that when observing White targets, participants judged anger as lasting longer on an old (M = 12.59s, SD = 4.24s) as compared to a young face (M = 11.31s, SD = 4.14 s), t(54) = -2.74, p = .008, d = -0.37. Thus, this replication was successful according to the SCORE criteria."

blind_target.authors: Kang, S. K., & Chasteen, A. L.
blind_target.title: Beyond the double-jeopardy hypothesis: Assessing emotion on the faces of multiply-categorizable targets of prejudice.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Claim Summary: This replication tests the claim from Kang et al. (2009) that for White

faces, participants would see anger appear sooner and linger longer on an old compared to a

young face, in line with research showing biases against White older adults, which reflects

the following statement from the paper's abstract: "Significant age by race interactions were

observed: while participants perceived anger as lasting longer and appearing sooner on old

compared to young White faces, this relationship was reversed for Black faces, with

participants perceiving anger lasting longer and appearing sooner on young compared to old

Black faces".
blind_target.outcome_quote:
For the happy-to-angry transition, analysis revealed a significant two-way interaction

between target age and target race, F(1, 54) = 4.07, p = .049, η²p = 0.07. When observing

Black targets, participants saw anger appear sooner on a young (M = 11.14 s, SD = 3.84 s)

as compared to an old face (M = 12.17, SD = 3.92 s), t(54) = -2.61, p = .012, d = -0.35. The

opposite, however not significant pattern was found for White targets, such that participants

judged anger as appearing sooner on an old (M = 10.68 s, SD = 3.38) as compared to a

young face (M = 13.34 s, SD = 12.70 s), t(54) = 1.47, p = .15. These results are not in line

with the original study and our stated hypotheses, which predicted that for White targets,

participants would judge anger as appearing significantly sooner on an old than on a young

face.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Focal angry-to-happy SCORE test explicitly succeeded, but report also explicitly contrasts other tested original findings: happy-to-angry White effect did not agree, angry-to-neutral Black effect was not fully in line, and neutral-to-angry Black direction was opposite. The success verdict is limited to the key SCORE claim/test, not an overall verdict covering all reported original comparisons. These explicit agreements and contrasts aggregate to mixed.

items.parent_scope_question: Distinguish key SCORE claim-specific verdict from all deliberately retested original comparisons; incidental explorations/checks need not enter aggregate outcome.
